clue.text: Disdain may have fine results

explanation.surface: A remark that contemptuous scorn can bring about pleasing outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like 'good', but it is a money penalty: contempt of court is punished with a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms; separately, a court may punish disrespect of its authority with a monetary penalty.

clue.text: 'Systematise reform of C.I.D."--Yard leader

indicators.note: reform means the letters of 'of C.I.D.' are formed again in a new order

parts.note: the word of and the initials of the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: leader picks the letter that heads the word Yard

explanation.surface: A call to overhaul the police detectives, from the head of Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges OFCID into CODIF, and 'leader' adds the Y that heads 'Yard'. The CID and Scotland Yard are London police names.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange laws or rules into a system is to make them orderly.

clue.text: In catechism, first answer to an inquiry ?

definitions.text: In catechism, first answer to an inquiry ?

parts.words: In catechism, first answer to an inquiry ?
parts.note: the Anglican catechism opens with 'What is your name?' and the printed reply is 'N. or M.', which sounds as a man's name

explanation.surface: Asks what the opening reply in a religious question-and-answer is.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Common Prayer catechism answers its first question with 'N or M', standing for the child's name; run together it is a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The catechism reply letters, joined, give a man's given name, and the first question asks for a name.

clue.text: Girl joins another artist, poor lad!

parts.note: another girl, here Esme
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters of lad are put in a bad state, a new order

explanation.surface: A girl takes up with a second woman and a painter, leaving a sad young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' gives a second girl's name, ESME; 'poor' rearranges LAD into LDA. Esmeralda is the heroine of The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is a woman's given name, famous from Victor Hugo's novel.

clue.text: He might make converts for the heathen-500, it's possible

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pagan is a heathen
D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: possible signals a possible arrangement of the letters of it's

parts.note: the letters of the word it's

explanation.surface: A missionary might win over unbelievers, five hundred perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A person spreading a doctrine seeks to win people over to it.

clue.text: Saint might appear to pine for the islands

definitions.text: Saint might appear to pine for the islands

parts.words: Saint might appear to pine for the islands
parts.note: an apostle's name followed by the word 'pines' spells the Asian island nation, so the saint seems to long ('pine') for those islands

explanation.surface: A holy figure looks homesick for some faraway archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pine' as the word PINES tacked on: the saint's name plus PINES gives the Philippines, the island country.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle of Jesus bore this name, which forms the first part of the name of the Asian island country.

clue.text: Girl of distinction in U.S.A.

explanation.surface: A distinguished young woman in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Honor is a girl's name, and also the American spelling of the word for esteem or distinction.

clue.text: Will make their fortune?

parts.note: a will is a legal testament, and it makes rich the people left money in it

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone called Will is going to make them rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a verb or a name, but it is the testament that leaves people money.
explanation.definitionFit: People left bequests in a testament are its beneficiaries.

clue.text: Hanger-on confounds one of 13

indicators.note: confounds means the letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: 13 across is aspirates, so one of them is an aspirate

explanation.surface: A sponger baffles one of thirteen people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of 13' points at 13 across: one of the ASPIRATES is an ASPIRATE, whose letters 'confounds' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who lives off others is called by the name of an organism that feeds on a host.

clue.text: Missile land in Devon ?

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile
a moor is a stretch of open uncultivated land

explanation.surface: A projectile comes down somewhere in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its great moorland is named after the river Dart.
explanation.definitionFit: The national park of upland heath in Devon is named after the river and its moor.

clue.text: Roe is upset about the horse, the ass !

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the horse word
upset means the letters of roe are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A deer is distressed over a horse, which turns out to be a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the horse, the ass' reads as two animals listed, but only 'the horse' is wordplay; 'the ass' is the definition, as the onager is a wild ass of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild species of donkey found in Asia.

clue.text: One noted for being honest and quiet

parts.note: an upright person is honest
piano is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone known for honesty and calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One noted' looks like a famous person, but it is an instrument that plays notes.
explanation.definitionFit: This keyboard instrument with vertical strings is something that produces musical notes.

clue.text: Fine about learner showing natural aptitude !

indicators.note: about here means the fine word goes around the learner letter

parts.note: fine weather is fair
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A good opinion of a student who shows a born talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is an instinctive talent or gift for something.

clue.text: Hopeless Hampshire openers sounded out of breath

definitions.text: Hopeless Hampshire openers sounded out of breath

parts.words: Hopeless Hampshire openers sounded out of breath
parts.note: the H that begins 'Hopeless' and 'Hampshire' is a breathed sound, and pronouncing it means sounding it with breath

explanation.surface: A poor county cricket side's opening batsmen are puffing and panting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tired cricketers (Hampshire is an English county with a cricket team); the clue is really about the letter H at the start of both words, a sound made with breath.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, sounding an H at the start of a word is to breathe it, which is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: National obligation to remain on top ?

definitions.text: National obligation to remain on top ?

parts.words: National obligation to remain on top ?
parts.note: a government's short-term borrowing is called by a word that also means staying on the surface of water

explanation.surface: Asks whether a country must stay ahead of the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remain on top' reads as staying in the lead, but it means staying on the surface of water, the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfunded short-term government borrowing is the economic term for this kind of public owing.

clue.text: Where these flowers are grown, I like to conclude

definitions.text: Where these flowers are grown, I like to conclude

indicators.note: to conclude means these pieces come at the end, after the garden

parts.note: plants are grown in a garden
as means like

explanation.surface: A gardener says where the blooms grow, adding a personal liking at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is an &lit: read whole, it also describes these scented white flowers and where they grow, while 'to conclude' places the last pieces at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenias are fragrant white-flowered shrubs grown in gardens.

clue.text: Small king takes blue material for vestment

parts.note: Chas is the short form of Charles, a king's name

indicators.note: material here signals the letters of blue being made into a new form

explanation.surface: A minor monarch picks blue cloth for his robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' means the abbreviated name CHAS; 'material' rearranges BLUE into UBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer garment a priest wears at Mass.

clue.text: Worrying hobby'?

parts.note: a pastime of cutting decorative patterns, whose name splits into a word for worrying and a word for labour

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pastime is a source of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: To fret is to worry, and the hobby of cutting ornamental patterns in wood is called by that word joined to 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental openwork cut with a fine saw is a well-known craft pastime.

clue.text: Sporadic localities

explanation.surface: Occasional places scattered about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring in scattered spots is irregular; as a phrase the words also name two places, near and far.

clue.text: Soldier upset over mutinous scene ? Take no notice !

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the soldier piece above the next one
upset in a down clue turns the soldier word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the Nore, an anchorage in the Thames estuary, was the scene of a naval mutiny in 1797

explanation.surface: A soldier is disturbed by a mutiny and told to disregard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GI into IG, placed 'over' NORE; the Nore mutiny of 1797 was in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention.

clue.text: Man leaves islands-women remain

indicators.note: leaves signals that the word for a man departs from the island name

parts.note: the Hebrides are islands off western Scotland
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man quits the islands while the women stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man, but it is HE, taken from HEBRIDES; 'remain' is a link to what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Brides are women about to marry or newly married.

clue.text: Pays for furniture before drink

indicators.note: before means the furniture word comes first, ahead of the drink

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench
to sup is to drink, or a sup is a mouthful

explanation.surface: Someone pays for the furnishings before having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; a settle is a wooden bench with a high back.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a bill or debt is to pay what is owed.

clue.text: Unfinished column edited by deputy

indicators.note: edited means the remaining letters are reworked into a new order
unfinished means the word column loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper column left incomplete is revised by a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts COLUMN to COLUM, and 'edited' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in for another, a temporary substitute.

clue.text: Composer of the "Laurel Garden ' pieces?

indicators.note: pieces signals that the answer is made of bits taken from inside the quoted title

explanation.surface: Asks who wrote a piece of music with a leafy garden title.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across laurEL GARden.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Brother Bill has one of 13 to open up

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
13 across is aspirates, and the letter H is an aspirate

explanation.surface: A monk named Bill holds an object he will open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of 13' points at 13 across, ASPIRATES: H is the aspirate. 'has' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject or a cask is to start discussing it or pierce it open.

clue.text: Pipe for the elderly male only ?

parts.note: a man is a male person
only, as in 'only if', is read as the conditional if
the elderly are old

explanation.surface: A tobacco pipe reserved for old gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'for the elderly male only' as a condition, man if old; the pieces come in a different order from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifold is a pipe or chamber with several branches, as on an engine's exhaust.

clue.text: He supplies the twist I smoke

indicators.note: a twist gives the letters of 'I smoke' a new order

explanation.surface: A man hands out the twist of tobacco I smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' looks like a twist of tobacco, but it tells you to rearrange I SMOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person of the Arctic peoples, so 'He' stands for one such man.

clue.text: They come into port. Vice versa on board

explanation.surface: Ships arrive in harbour, and the reverse happens aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Small trading ships come into port; and on a board (a table) the port wine comes onto them, the reverse of coming into port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships plying along a coastline are so called, as are the mats that glasses of port are set on at table.
